reason: The cited evidence does not address grain-boundary diffusion of Cr in duplex steels, the effect of grain size on passivation, or the self-healing of Cr-rich films. E1 notes Cr vulnerability in fluoride salts, E2 discusses high-entropy alloys, and E3 shows a different alloy (AlCoCrFeNi2.1) outperforming DS2205 due to Al sacrificial effects, not grain refinement. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Grain refinement increases grain-boundary density in duplex stainless steels
Higher grain-boundary density accelerates Cr diffusion to the surface
Accelerated Cr diffusion promotes formation of a Cr-rich passive film
A Cr-rich passive film reduces corrosion in aggressive environments
Ultrafine-grained duplex steels will show shallower Cr depletion and lower corrosion rates than coarse-grained counterparts
